Maya K: Hitting SSL cert verify errors with Python SDK on Windows (py3.11) venv, works on linux and older py3.9.
Maya K: Example failure when creating client + simple request:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "example.py", line 42, in <module>
    resp = client.text.generate(...)
  File ".../site-packages/requests/sessions.py", line 614, in get
    resp = self.request('GET', url, **kwargs)
requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:997)
```
Maya K: Env: Windows 11, python.org 3.11.4, venv created with `py -3.11 -m venv .venv`, sdk 0.7.0. Company proxy in use; proxy cert is installed in Windows cert store.
Shiv P: Do we know which ssl backend/bundled openssl is used? python.org builds may link OpenSSL; that affects cert store precedence.
Maya K: `ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION` shows OpenSSL 3.0.10. Behavior: py3.9 on same machine succeeds, py3.11 fails consistently.
Alice L: Quick workaround: install certifi and set SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where() or supply an ssl.SSLContext with cafile=certifi.where().
Ben T: Example programmatic workaround:
```python
import ssl, certifi
ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
# If SDK accepts ssl_context param
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., ssl_context=ctx)
# Or for requests session fallback:
session = requests.Session()
session.verify = certifi.where()
```
Ben T: If that fixes it, we should make the SDK prefer explicit SSL_CERT_FILE, then certifi, then system defaults, and accept ssl_context for both sync + async clients.
Maya K: Setting SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where() fixed my repro. Confirmed: cert resolution precedence issue.
Maya K: Minimal repro I ran:
```python
import requests, ssl, certifi, platform, sys
print(platform.platform(), sys.version)
print('openssl', ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION)
print('certifi', certifi.where())
requests.get('https://example.com')
```
# raises on 3.11, succeeds on 3.9

Shiv P: Filing a bug is good. Short-term: docs quickstart addition for Windows and add ssl_context param to async client.
Shiv P: @Alice L can you draft the quickstart blurb?
Alice L: Draft: "If you hit CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED on Windows, install certifi and set SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where() or pass ssl.SSLContext(cafile=certifi.where()) to the client." I'll open a docs PR.
Ben T: Working on an HTTP-layer change to prefer SSL_CERT_FILE then certifi then system, plus AsyncClient signature: `ssl_context: Optional[ssl.SSLContext] = None`. Will update type stubs and run mypy.
Shiv P: Drop PR link so QE can test across py3.8-3.12 on Win/Linux.
Ben T: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/215 - adds ssl_context passthrough, certifi precedence, and typing updates.
Maya K: Built a wheel from that branch and tested on my 3.11 venv - issue resolved. No SSLError. Thanks!
Maya K: I'll attach repro steps to INF-3421 and keep this thread open until docs + patch release.
